month_outlook: A dark, wet, sniffly November is about to collide with your comfort-buying reflex. Watch 14-23 Nov.

threats.title: The Ten-Day Downpour Takeaway Spiral
threats.local_signal: Yellow rain warning for 14-23 Nov, plus delivery apps waiving fees on rainy evenings.
threats.psych_trigger: When you're exhausted and the weather is grey, you buy comfort and have it delivered.
threats.prediction: Ten wet days take away the option of going out, and the fee waivers take away the friction. Expect 6-9 delivery orders in one week.
threats.countermeasure: Batch-cook or buy 5 freezer meals this Sunday and label them 'storm week'. Log out of delivery apps on 13 Nov.

threats.title: The Black Friday Low-Mood Basket
threats.local_signal: Low-mood referrals are up 30%, and Black Friday deals start on 13 Nov.
threats.psych_trigger: Low mood in the evening, plus lifestyle inflation ('I deserve that').
threats.prediction: In the low-daylight weeks, late-night browsing turns into 'treat yourself' buys like cosy clothes, skincare and gadgets, mostly after 9pm.
threats.countermeasure: Set a 9pm limit on shopping apps, and buy a light-therapy lamp now (£35). It costs less than the low moods it prevents.

threats.title: The Replacement-Bus Taxi Tax
threats.local_signal: Tram lines are part-closed 10-23 Nov and surge pricing is expected, all during an early flu wave.
threats.psych_trigger: You don't tolerate discomfort well when you're tired, so you pay to make the hassle go away.
threats.prediction: Rain and 40-minute bus detours push you into surge-priced taxis 2-3 times a week, especially on days you're ill or running late.
threats.countermeasure: Buy a weekly bus pass in advance and set a rule: only take a taxi if it saves you 2 hours or more. Stock up on cold remedies before the shortage.
